name: Huzhou Museum
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Huzhou lists it with hours and three permanent exhibitions; a city museum visitors can tour for an hour.
objection: A provincial-level comprehensive city museum is an ordinary stop; Chinese-only labels likely.

name: Huzhou Art Museum
reason: Rule 1-2: one Wikivoyage listing (daily 09:00-16:30), Greek-style building with calligraphy and relics; a plausible half-hour stop.
objection: Single counted source, no page views; another municipal gallery, only for visitors already in Huzhou city.

name: Huzhou Science and Technology Museum
reason: Rule 1-2: one Wikivoyage listing; open Wed-Sun by online booking, kid-oriented aerospace exhibits.
objection: Local children's science centre, booking in Chinese, not a draw for travellers from elsewhere.

name: Huzhou Brush Museum
reason: Rule 1-2: Zhejiang tourism (ct.zj.gov.cn China Hubi Museum) and China Daily Huzhou name it; Huzhou brush is one of the Four Treasures of the study and the museum has a Zhao Mengfu hall.
objection: Sources disagree on location (Lianhuazhuang vs Shanlian town) so the pin needs checking; niche craft museum.

name: Zhao Mengfu Former Residence Memorial
reason: Rule 1-3: China Daily Huzhou and huzhou.gov.cn describe a 4,500 sq m memorial hall to the Yuan calligrapher, open since 2012.
objection: Largely reconstructed; overlaps the Zhao Mengfu hall in the Brush Museum and Lianhuazhuang Park, so may be a near-duplicate.

name: Lianhuazhuang Park
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Huzhou lists it (06:00-20:00), lotus pond and old trees on Zhao Mengfu's garden site; a half-hour stroll beside the Brush Museum.
objection: Largely a 1980s reconstruction; an urban park.

name: Xishan Yang Wetland
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage describes it as Huzhou's answer to West Lake with wetland park and painting academy.
objection: One source, thin detail, a local leisure area on the city edge.

name: Huzhou Changdao Park
reason: Rule 3 negative benchmark: an ordinary urban park Wikivoyage recommends for exercise; spring tulips are seasonal.
objection: Largest park in the city and a Wikivoyage listing, so a visitor may stroll it; but nothing a traveller goes out of their way for.

name: Taihu Lake Amusement Park
reason: Rule 1-2: a permanent amusement and water park on the Taihu shore (Longemont-type resort), but only travel-site evidence found, no counted source.
objection: Operator-run theme park with no visitor-guide source; may be the same venue as the Taihu Lake Tourist Resort entries.

name: Zhili
reason: Rule 2: a children's-clothing wholesale town, nothing for a visitor to do.
objection: None; the wholesale market is not a visitor sight.

name: Qianshanyang Site
reason: Rule 1-2: Neolithic silk-fragment site; no visitor source found and public access unconfirmed.
objection: The finds are in the Zhejiang silk museum; likely a bare field.

name: Meishan Section (Permian-Triassic boundary)
reason: Rule 1-2: IUGS geoheritage Permian-Triassic golden spike at Changxing with a museum and geopark; no tourism-board source found.
objection: Of interest mainly to geologists; opening and access unconfirmed.

name: Jiaye Tang
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Nanxun; a famous private library and garden visitors tour inside.
objection: Part of Nanxun ancient town's ticketing; keep as it is a distinct gated site.

name: Former Residence of Zhang Shiming
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Nanxun; walk-in merchant mansion mixing Chinese courtyards with French stained glass.
objection: One of many Nanxun mansions; could be treated as part of the town.

name: Former Residence of Zhang Jingjiang
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage Nanxun lists Zunde Hall as a late-Qing residence open to visitors.
objection: Another Nanxun mansion, near-duplicate of Zhang Shiming's, little to distinguish for a foreign visitor.

name: Red House (Liu Ansheng Residence)
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Nanxun; Jiangnan facade with a European ballroom interior.
objection: Near-duplicate of the other Nanxun mansions.

name: Qiushuli Villa
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Nanxun; 1930 East-West villa by the Jiaye Library owner.
objection: Minor villa in the Jiaye precinct; likely part of the Jiaye Tang visit.

name: Jili Silk Exhibition Hall
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Nanxun; silk exhibition in the former Chamber of Commerce, tied to Nanxun's silk heritage.
objection: Small exhibition hall, possibly the same building as the Silk Guild Hall.

name: Baijianlou
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Nanxun; riverside Ming houses with sunrise views, also named in the Huzhou district overview.
objection: A row of houses on the town's canal, part of the town itself.

name: Little Lotus Garden
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Nanxun and Huzhou; 'First Private Garden in Jiangnan', a walk-in garden of an hour.
objection: Within the Nanxun scenic area.

name: Yingyuan Garden
reason: Rule 1: only an OSM viewpoint tag; no visitor source found that names it as a stop.
objection: Could be a real Nanxun garden; not evidenced.

name: Guanghui Palace
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Nanxun lists the Taoist temple by Guanghui Bridge.
objection: Small temple, one source, adds little beyond the town walk.

name: Tongjin Bridge
reason: Rule 3: a bridge within Nanxun ancient town, which is itself a spot; part of a larger spot.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it and it is the centre of the old silk trade, but it is seen in passing.

name: Hongji Bridge
reason: Rule 3: a Qing arch bridge within Nanxun, part of the larger town spot; a minor stop.
objection: 15k page views and a listing, but visitors cross it while walking the town.

name: Guanghui Bridge
reason: Rule 3: another Nanxun bridge, part of the larger town spot.
objection: A protected relic, but a quick look.

name: Nanxun Night Tour and Boat Ride
reason: COVERAGE 'A spot is a place': a boat ride and evening tour, the place is Nanxun.
objection: A popular evening activity, but belongs in the Nanxun bio.

name: Nanxun Christian Church
reason: Rule 2: a church with no visitor source naming anything to see inside.
objection: Could have notable architecture; unsourced.

name: Yunxiu Temple
reason: Rule 1: Wikipedia category tag only; no visitor source.
objection: Unknown location and visitor interest, not searched beyond candidate.

name: Digang Ancient Village
reason: Rule 1-2: one Wikivoyage Huzhou listing for a thousand-year-old village with an original street, few tourists.
objection: Little known and the listing itself calls it quiet; second-tier at best.

name: Linghu Ancient Town
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Huzhou lists Ming-Qing houses, bridges and canals, open 24 hours.
objection: Quiet and little documented; a second water town beside Nanxun.

name: Anji Bamboo Exposition Park
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Anji names it as the county centrepiece with a bamboo museum and a panda house.
objection: Themed park with a family bias.

name: Anji Panda House
reason: Rule 3: a feature inside Anji Bamboo Exposition Park, part of a larger spot.
objection: Pandas draw visitors, but the park is the place.

name: China Bamboo Museum
reason: Rule 3: inside the Anji Bamboo Exposition Park, part of the larger spot.
objection: A museum is a distinct visit, but it shares the park's gate.

name: Great Bamboo Sea (Anji)
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Anji and Huzhou name it (Wuhe village, Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon film location); an obvious draw with two counted sources.
objection: Remote by minibus and a bus transfer; the name is also used for other bamboo forests in the county.

name: Silver Diggings Under Heaven
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Anji lists a former silver mine and film-set scenic area with tunnels, 07:00-17:00.
objection: One source; a movie-set theme attraction needing taxi access.

name: Dragon King Mountain
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Anji lists it (CNY 70), a mountain scenic area with no public transport.
objection: Hard to reach and thin detail in the listing.

name: Baicaoyuan Garden
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Anji lists a large man-made garden with mini-zoo and swimming beach (CNY 150).
objection: Family leisure park, high price, mostly amusements.

name: Zhejiang Museum of Natural History Anji Branch
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Anji lists the museum with geology, dinosaur and ecology halls and opening hours.
objection: Next to Baicaoyuan and aimed at families; a one-source listing.

name: Hello Kitty Park
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Anji lists the permanent Hello Kitty theme park with bus access and hours.
objection: Operator-run theme park aimed at children; one source.

name: Xiao Hangkeng
reason: Rule 2-3: a lakeside campsite described only in a user-written line; no sight or activity of its own.
objection: Pleasant lawn and bamboo view, but it is a camp.

name: Jiangnan Tianchi
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Anji names the AAAA scenic area at Tianhuangping (also called Tianchi River), with a lake and planetarium; nearby Great Bamboo Sea draws.
objection: The listing reads as promotional copy; one source.

name: Tianhuangping
reason: Rule 3: a town acting as base; its sights (Great Bamboo Sea, Silver Diggings, Tianchi) are listed separately.
objection: A base for several scenic areas and could stand as a town spot, but nothing there of its own.

name: Canglong Baipu
reason: Rule 1-2: Zhejiang Dept of Culture and Tourism (ct.zj.gov.cn) and China Daily Huzhou describe the largest waterfall cluster in northern Zhejiang, a gorge walk with cableway.
objection: Only promotional sources; opening hours vary between listings.

name: Shangmakan Paleolithic Site
reason: Rule 2: an archaeological site with no visitor source and no confirmed public access.
objection: May have a small exhibit, unverified.

name: Fushi Reservoir
reason: Rule 1: no visitor source names it as a stop; Xiao Hangkeng is the camp by it.
objection: A scenic reservoir, but only OSM evidence.

name: Moganshan Villa Cluster
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Moganshan; about 150 early 20th-century villas set in bamboo forest.
objection: Part of the wider Mount Mogan scenic area, but the villas are a distinct draw visitors walk to.

name: Sword Pool Waterfall (Jianchi)
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Moganshan; canyon waterfalls and pools below the village with the sword-casting legend.
objection: Ticket is the Moganshan entry ticket; part of the mountain area.

name: Tashan Forest Park
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Huzhou lists it for morning walks near Tashan town on Mount Mogan.
objection: Generic forest park, one source.

name: Lu Hua Dang Park
reason: Rule 1-2: reed-marsh park on Moganshan (芦花荡公园); no counted source found in this run's search.
objection: Only a candidate-file mention; may be within the main scenic area.

name: Land Rover Experience Huzhou
reason: COVERAGE 'A spot is a place': an operator's off-road driving experience; Wikivoyage link dead.
objection: Operator activity next to Naked Retreats, not a place.

name: Xiazhu Lake
reason: Rule 1-2: Zhejiang Dept of Culture and Tourism (ct.zj.gov.cn) and China Daily government pages describe a 4A wetland park with crested-ibis base and reed-maze boat trips.
objection: Out in Deqing and hours conflict between listings; bird sightings are not guaranteed.

name: Fangfeng Mountain
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Huzhou names Fangfeng culture and the mountain in Deqing, but only the temple fair is listed.
objection: The listed draw is an event; nothing confirmed for a regular visit.

name: Fangfeng Temple
reason: Rule 1-2: the temple is permanent though Wikivoyage lists only its annual temple fair; same place as Fangfeng Mountain.
objection: The only sourced hook is the fair; near-duplicate of the mountain.

name: Xianshan Lake Scenic Area
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Huzhou names it among Changxing's attractions; lakeside scenic area at Si'an reservoir.
objection: Thin detail, one source.

name: Shuikou Tea Culture Tourism Scenic Area
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Huzhou names it among Changxing's attractions; a 4A tea-culture area (Trip.com).
objection: Pin is the town centre only; tea tourism of one source.

name: Chinese Alligator Village
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Huzhou names it among Changxing's attractions; a breeding park with Chinese alligators.
objection: A captive-breeding attraction, one source.

name: Gu Zhu Mountain
reason: Rule 1-2: huzhou.gov.cn place-of-interest and China Daily describe the Tang Tribute Tea Academy museum on Gu Zhu Mountain, tied to Lu Yu's Classic of Tea.
objection: Pin should sit at the Tribute Tea Academy, not the mountain; visitor admission details unconfirmed.

name: Taiji Cave
reason: Rule 1: the English Taiji Cave is in Anhui; no Huzhou cave found by search, so the entity is unverified.
objection: The zh Wikipedia link may refer to a real Huzhou cave that I could not confirm.

name: Duihekou Reservoir
reason: Rule 1: no visitor source; OSM Wikipedia tag only. Not individually searched.
objection: A scenic reservoir with a possible walk.

name: Siling Reservoir
reason: Rule 1: no visitor source; OSM tag only. Not individually searched.
objection: A scenic reservoir with a possible walk.

name: Laoshikan Reservoir
reason: Rule 1: no visitor source; OSM tag only. Not individually searched.
objection: A scenic reservoir with a possible walk.

name: Nanxun Catholic Church
reason: Rule 2: a church with no visitor source naming anything to see.
objection: Might hold interior interest; unsourced.

name: Jishan Bamboo Sea
reason: Rule 1-3: OSM only, near-duplicate of the Great Bamboo Sea.
objection: A separate forest might exist; no source.

name: Crouching Tiger Filming Site Monument
reason: Rule 3: a plaque-style memorial inside the Great Bamboo Sea.
objection: Film fans stop there, but it is within the bamboo sea.

name: Nanxun Silk Guild Hall
reason: Rule 3: probably the same building as Jili Silk Exhibition Hall.
objection: Could be distinct; no source.

name: Guzhu Reservoir (Bawang Pool)
reason: Rule 1,3: Bawang Pool is part of the Gu Zhu scenic area, a reservoir with no source.
objection: Named in the Gu Zhu scenic area description.

name: Huzhou Taihu Lake Moon Hot Spring Resort
reason: Rule 1-2: a large hot-spring bathing venue (Trip.com's top hot spring in Huzhou, supporting only); visitors can spend hours, but no counted source.
objection: A hotel-linked spa, not a sight; operator-run.

name: Taihu Lake Tourist Resort
reason: Rule 1-3: Trip.com lists it (Taihu Longemont Paradise, hot springs, water park, circus); a resort district, not one place.
objection: A district bundling several operator venues, overlapping Taihu Tuying and the amusement park; no counted source.

name: Taihu Tuying Resort
reason: Rule 1-2: Trip.com and a Wyndham local-area list name Taihu Tuying Ecology Wetland Culture Park in Changxing; counted source not found.
objection: May duplicate Taihu Lake Tourist Resort; operator-run.

name: Wu Changshuo Memorial Hall
reason: Rule 1-2: huzhou China Daily pages describe the Anji hall in Changshuo Park with the artist's residence, statue and works; a memorial museum, not a plaque.
objection: Wu Changshuo is revered in China but display labels are likely Chinese-only; guide-source evidence is China Daily only.

name: Yunshang Grassland Starry Sky Ski Resort
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Anji calls it the closest natural ski resort to Hangzhou and China Daily reported it opening Dec 2025; a permanent ski field (grass skiing in summer).
objection: Operator-run, new, 1,168 m with seasonal snow.

name: Anji Yucun
reason: Rule 1-2: China Daily Huzhou government page presents Yucun, a UN Tourism Best Tourism Village, with village walks, bamboo crafts, Future Village hall and Hidden-Dragon Waterfall; open 24 h, a half-day stop.
objection: Overlaps in area with Tianhuangping/Jiangnan Tianchi and Anji Bamboo Expo Park; busy weekends.

name: Tianmu Lake
reason: Rule 1: the Tianmu Lake tourist resort named by visitor sources is in Liyang, Changzhou, Jiangsu, not Huzhou; no Huzhou counted source names a lake of that name (Anji's Jiangnan Tianchi is already listed).
objection: If a Huzhou-side reservoir is meant, it is a local reservoir with no visitor source found.

name: Changxing Taihu Museum
reason: Rule 1-2: only travel-platform listings found (free, 7 floors, lake-view top floor, 09:00-16:30), no Wikivoyage/tourism-board page; a real, open museum.
objection: For: free, notable building on the lakeshore, pairs with Taihu Ancient Town. Against: one non-counted source, a standard county museum.

name: Xinshi Ancient Town
reason: Rule 1-2: China Daily Huzhou government pages describe this Deqing water town, promoted to a provincial 5A tourist attraction, with old streets and canals to walk.
objection: Another Jiangnan water town beside Nanxun and Wuzhen; crowds and shops.

name: Yishang Street Historical and Cultural Block
reason: Rule 1: one China Daily Huzhou item (national historic and cultural block with intangible heritage); old-street walk in Huzhou city.
objection: For: named national block. Against: single counted source, short visit, possibly redeveloped shops.

name: Anji Ancient City National Archaeological Site Park
reason: Rule 1-2: one China Daily Huzhou item (cherry blossom park at the Anji ancient city site); open site park.
objection: For: public park on an archaeological site. Against: little to see beyond seasonal blossom, one source.

name: Taihu Lake Longemont Paradise
reason: Rule 1-2: China Daily Huzhou names it a national nighttime tourism zone with Nanxun; an operator-run theme-park resort.
objection: For: named nighttime culture zone. Against: operator theme park, details thin.
